--- title: "INLA and Beyond: Bayesian Hierarchical modelling with `inlabru`" subtitle: "30/11/2026 • UNAM, México
Jafet Belmont · Sara Martino · Janine Illian" title-block-banner: "#00000000" title-block-banner-color: "white" format: html: css: styles.css body-classes: home-page PrettyPDF-pdf: keep-tex: true number-sections: true editor_options: chunk_output_type: console params: city: "UNAM, CDMX" country: "Mexico" year: 2026 month: "November" days: "30th" base_url: "https://inlabru-courses.github.io/MExico_2026/" --- # Welcome to the course! - Welcome to the `inlabru` workshop! - Over one day, we'll introduce Bayesian hierarchical modelling with `inlabru`, focusing on spatial models for ecological data. - The day alternates short lectures with hands-on practicals. - Workshop materials are available in the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/inlabru-courses/ISEC2027). ::: {.callout-warning} ## Important! ⚠️ Please use the instructions provided [here](Install_software.qmd) to install and check your installation *before* the course starts. ::: # Learning objectives By the end of the workshop, participants will be able to: - **specify, fit and interpret** Bayesian hierarchical models in `inlabru`; - **explain** why hierarchical (latent Gaussian) models are relevant in spatial ecology, and how `inlabru` fits them with INLA; - **build** spatial models — continuous fields (SPDE) and point processes (LGCP) — and **map** their predictions; # Intended audience The workshop aims to cater for participants with a range of different backgrounds, who are interested in analysing data with modern spatial statistical modelling approaches. # Prerequisites Participants should be familiar with the `R` environment, and general statistical approaches for modelling such as regression, analysis of (co)variance, and generalized linear models. No knowledge of `R-INLA` or `inlabru` is required. # Schedule {#schedule-tabs} ::: {.text-center} #### Morning Session ::: | Time | Topic | |:----------------------------------:|:----------------------------------:| | 9:00 - 9:15 | [**Welcome and introduction to the course**](slides/welcome.html) | | 9:15 - 10:00 | [**Session 1**: Introduction to `inlabru`](slides/slides_1.html) | 1| 10:00 - 10:45 | [Practical Session 1](practicals/LMM_ex.qmd) | | 10:45 - 11:15 | [**Session 2**: The `inlabru` workflow](slides/slides_2.html) | | 11:15 - 12:00 | [Practical Session 2](practicals/GLMM_fit.qmd) | ::: {.text-center} #### Afternoon Session ::: | Time | Topic | |:----------------------------------:|:----------------------------------:| | 15:00 - 15:45 | [**Session 3**: Geostatistics and the SPDE approach](slides/slides_geostats.html) | | 15:45 - 16:15 | [Practical Session 3](practicals/Geostat_ex.qmd) | | 16:15 - 17:00 | [**Session 4**: Point Processes](slides/slides_points.html) | | 17:00 - 17:30 | [Practical Session 4](day3_practical_5.html)| | 17:30 - 18:00 | [Closing session](slides/slides_Closing_Remarks.html) and discussion | # Licence [CC-BY-4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) # Citation ```{=html}
